title: Browser evidence
description: A record of what a browser run actually exercised, produced by a tool this repository does not ship (ADR 0002). This schema validates SHAPE ONLY. Whether the run's identity is fresh, whether its coverage is complete, and whether a given check establishes a given rule are separate questions answered by scripts/evidence.mjs and scripts/compliance.mjs — run completion, coverage, freshness, and check outcome are four independent axes, and no one of them implies another. A producer may not establish a rule by asserting it: every claim here is either recomputed against the repository or scoped to the route and viewport it was observed on.

producedBy.description: Which tool produced this record. Named so that a finding can be traced to the thing that made it, and so a producer's own defects are attributable.

revision.description: What source this run observed. `sourceIdentity` is recomputed from the committed tree at `gitSha` — a producer cannot supply an identity from one revision alongside the SHA of another, because the identity is never taken on trust (ADR 0011).

gitSha.description: A full commit SHA. A branch name or tag would re-point over time, leaving no historical subject to reconstruct.

paths.description: The UI paths this run's identity covers. Where the policy declares `ui.evidencePaths`, these must match it exactly: a producer that narrows the subject would otherwise be able to widen its own claim by measuring less.

run.description: Whether the PRODUCER finished. This says nothing about whether the evidence is complete enough to establish any particular rule — that is coverage, and it is a different axis.

viewports.description: The viewports this run could exercise, each mapped to one of the project's declared viewport classes so that coverage is comparable against `ui.viewportClasses`.

routes.description: One entry per route the run enumerated. A route the run did not reach is recorded with status `failed` or `skipped` and establishes nothing; omitting it instead would make an unexercised route indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

check.description: One rule's outcome at one route and viewport. `inconclusive` is a first-class outcome and establishes nothing — it exists so that a producer never has to choose between claiming a pass it cannot support and staying silent about having looked.

ruleId.description: A canonical catalog rule id. Byte-identical to CANONICAL_ID in scripts/catalog.mjs and to $defs/ruleId in project-policy.schema.json — three spellings of one grammar would be three identities.
